tip: Εσείς (eseis) and the -ετε (-ete) of έχετε (echete) are the polite-or-plural 'you': one person you respect, or several people.
σχολείο goes bare: πάει σχολείο (pai scholio) has no 'to' and no 'the' – like English 'goes home', but for school.
Αυτή (afti) is 'this one' for feminine words – it matches γυναίκα (gynaika = woman/wife). A neuter word would take αυτό (afto).
Του (tou = his) follows the noun: η γυναίκα του (i gynaika tou), literally 'the wife his'.

target: Ναι, το κλειδί είναι στην τσάντα.
english: Yes, the key is in the bag.
tip: Στην (stin) is σε (se) + την (tin) squeezed together: στην τσάντα (stin tsanta) = in the bag. Greek always contracts σε (se) with 'the'.
Greek 'the' changes with gender: η (i) goes with feminine words like η βαλίτσα (i valitsa = the suitcase).

english: The book is at the office.
tip: Το (to) is the neuter 'the': το βιβλίο (to vivlio = the book). Στο (sto) = σε (se) + το (to), 'at the'.
Ο (o) is the masculine 'the': ο υπολογιστής (o ypologistis = the computer). The adjective matches too: παλιός (palios = old).
Greek has one present tense: τρώει (troi) covers both 'eats' and 'is eating'. τώρα (tora = now) supplies the -ing feel.
No 'do' helper for negation – δεν (den) before the verb does the whole job: Δεν έχω αυτοκίνητο (den echo aftokinito), 'not I-have car'.

target: Αυτό δεν είναι το τηλέφωνό μου.
tip: Αυτό (afto) is 'this one' for neuter words – it points at το τηλέφωνό μου (to tilefono mou = my phone).
'A' changes form as the object: ένας (enas) becomes έναν (enan) when the coffee is what you want – Θέλω έναν καφέ (thelo enan kafe).
Masculine 'the' switches ο (o) to τον (ton) when the noun is the object: θέλουμε τον λογαριασμό (theloume ton logariasmo).

target: Θέλω ένα εισιτήριο για την Αθήνα.
english: I want a ticket to Athens.
tip: Place names carry the article: για την Αθήνα (gia tin Athina) is literally 'for the Athens'.
Να (na) links verbs where English uses 'to': θέλω να πάω (thelo na pao = I want to go). Greek chains verbs with να (na), not a 'to' form.

target: Θέλω να μιλάω ελληνικά κάθε μέρα.
english: I want to speak Greek every day.
tip: Greek has no 'to speak' form. After θέλω you conjugate again with να: Θέλω να μιλάω (thelo na milao) is literally 'I want that I speak'.

english: Do you want us to go for coffee?
tip: The verb after να (na) carries its own person: θέλεις να πάμε (theleis na pame) = you want US to go – πάμε (pame) already says 'us'.

target: Αυτό το βιβλίο είναι πολύ καλό.
tip: 'This X' keeps 'the': αυτό το βιβλίο (afto to vivlio) is literally 'this the book' – the article never drops.
'This' doesn't replace 'the' – Greek stacks them: Αυτή η τσάντα (afti i tsanta) is literally 'this the bag'.
'This' agrees in gender: your aunt is feminine, so αυτή (afti). A man would be αυτός (aftos), a thing αυτό (afto).

target: Αυτό το τρένο πάει στην Αθήνα;
english: Does this train go to Athens?
tip: Cities keep their article: στην Αθήνα (stin Athina) is literally 'to the Athens'. Greek place names almost always carry 'the'.

target: Δεν θέλω το μεγάλο δωμάτιο, θέλω το μικρό.
english: I don't want the big room, I want the small one.
tip: Article + adjective stands alone: θέλω το μικρό (thelo to mikro) = I want the small one. Greek has no word for 'one' here.

english: What do you do in the morning?
tip: Τι κάνεις; (Ti kanis) on its own is the greeting 'how are you?'. Adding a topic like το πρωί (to proi = in the morning) turns it back into a real 'what do you do?'.
The accent matters: πού (pou) with an accent asks 'where'; unaccented που (pou) means 'that/which'.
'Who' matches gender: ποιος (poios) for masculine like ο γιατρός (o giatros), ποια (poia) feminine, ποιο (poio) neuter.

english: How do you get to work?
tip: The accent flips the meaning: πώς (pos) asks 'how', as in πώς πας (pos pas = how do you get there); unaccented πως (pos) means 'that'.
'Which' has gender: ποια (poia) is feminine to match αδερφή (aderfi = sister). Asking about a brother, you'd switch to ποιος (poios).
Swap the little word to ask about others: πώς τον λένε (pos ton lene) is literally 'how do they call him' – what's his name.

target: Πώς το λέτε αυτό στα ελληνικά;
english: How do you say this in Greek?
tip: Languages take στα (sta): στα ελληνικά (sta elliniká = in Greek), στα αγγλικά (sta angliká = in English).
Πόσο (póso) before a describing word asks 'how': πόσο μακριά; (póso makriá = how far?), πόσο μεγάλο (póso megálo = how big).
